questions.question: Which of the following styles of temple architecture was developed between Himalaya to Vindhya?
questions.solution:
__**Nagara styles**__ of temple architecture was developed between Himalaya to Vindhya

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**** ****Nagara or North Indian Temple Style**

__
 
• In North India, it is common for an entire temple to be built on a** stone platform with steps leading up to it.**
 
• It does not usually have elaborate b**oundary walls or gateways.**
 
• While the earliest temples had just **one tower or shikhara**, later temples had several.
 
• The **garbhagriha **is always located directly under the tallest tower.
 
• There are many subdivisions of nagara temples depending on the shape of the **shikhara.**
 
• The second major type of architectural form in the nagara order is the **phamsana**, which tends to be broader and shorter than Latina ones.
 
• Their roofs are composed of several slabs that gently rise to a single point over the center of the building, unlike the Latina ones which look like sharply rising tall towers.
 
• The third main sub-type of the nagara building is generally called the **valabhi type**.
 
• These are rectangular buildings with a roof that rises into a **vaulted chamber**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Dravida Or South Indian Temple Style**

 
• Unlike the nagara temple, the Dravida temple is enclosed within a compound wall.
 
• The front wall has an entrance gateway in its center, which is known as a **gopuram**.
 
• The shape of the main temple tower known as** vimana in Tamil Nadu **is like a stepped pyramid that rises up geometrically rather than the curving shikhara of North India.
 
• It is common to find a large **water reservoir, or a temple tank, enclosed within the complex.**
 
• Subsidiary shrines are either incorporated within the main temple tower or located as distinct, separate small shrines beside the main temple.
 
• **Kanchipuram, Thanjavur or Tanjore, Madurai, and Kumbakonam are the most famous temple towns of Tamil Nadu, **where, during the 8th-12th centuries, the role of the temple was not limited to religious matters alone.

questions.question: Select the FALSE statement with reference to the food chain.

options.text: Inter-relation between different food chains is known as a food web.
All the chains formed by nutritional relations is used to understand energy flow.
Only producers of food chain form a trophic level.
Every component of the food chain forms a trophic level.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only producers of the food chain form a trophic level.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• There are unique interactions and relationships which are involved in the transportation of energy.
 
• The energy, once produced and captured, is distributed throughout the various living organisms.
 
• **This transfer of energy is termed the food web.**
 
• In specialized terms, Food Chain is the sequence through which the transfer of energy takes place within a particular ecosystem.
 
• **Energy transfer is pivotal for the survival and food of living organisms.**
 
• Trophic position refers to the successional stages in a food chain, starting with directors at the bottom, followed by primary, secondary, and tertiary consumers.
 
• **Every position in a food chain is known as a trophic position**. ***Hence, the Option 3 is Incorrect.​***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76869f6f1f571bea548e433fe63b566a3e342b4b9e645e1165b8cdd2f3d1edd4.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6dd88533bd479397c8ff098b2f7d94cd87266b920004f4f2f9d17ef4fb30dd9b.png] 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• Both food chains and food webs, share three types of organisms in a food chain:** Producers, Consumers, and decomposers**.

 
 
• **Producers:** The producers in a food chain include all autotrophs such as phytoplankton.

 
 
• This is the first stage in a food chain.
 
• The producers make up the first level of a food chain.
 
 
 
• **Consumers:** Consumers are all organisms that are dependent on plants or other organisms for food.
 
 
• This is the largest part of a food web, as it contains almost all living organisms.
 
• It includes herbivores which are animals that eat plants, carnivores which are animals that eat other animals, parasites that live on other organisms by harming them, and lastly scavengers, which are animals that eat dead animals’ carcasses.
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:** Decomposers are organisms that get energy from dead or waste organic material.
 
 
• This is the last stage in a food chain.
 
• Decomposers are an integral part of a food chain, as they convert organic waste materials into inorganic materials, which enriches the soil or land with nutrients.

questions.question: Which scientist explained that cells divide and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudolf Virchow.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Rudolf Virchow expanded the cell theory and suggested that **all the cells arise from pre-existing cells.**
 
• The cell theory, given by **Rudolf Virchow in 1855**, states that:
 
 
• All living organisms are made up of cells.
 
• The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.
 
• All cells arise from pre-existing cells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Theodore Schwann**

 
• He was a **British Zoologist who in 1839, studied different types of animal cells.**
 
• On the basis of this, Schwann proposed the hypothesis that the bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.

**Anton Van Leeuwenhoek**

 
• He is known as **"the Father of Microbiology"**.
 
• He discovered "protozoa" - the single-celled organisms. 

**Robert Hooke**

 
• **He discovered cells by observing them in a cork slice** in 1665.
 
• Under a microscope, he could only see honey- comb-like structures in a slice of cork.
 
• Since that was a dead tissue, he could only see the cell walls.
 
• **He thus coined the term ‘Cell’.**

• **A bowed stringed instrument with a resonator covered in skin is called a sarangi.**
 
• Typically, a **single block of wood** is used to handcraft a sarangi.
 
• The seventeen sympathetic strings on this instrument are constructed of steel, while the four playing strings are made of goat gut.
 
• The sarangi is a common instrument in India with numerous regional variations, but it plays a significant role in the Hindustani music of North India.
 
• The sarangi is the only musical instrument that can accurately produce all of the nuances of vocal music, including khayal, dhrupad, khayal, thumri, tappa, ghazal, and even bhajan, with embellishments and intonations.

**Sitar**

 
• **Sitar is a plucked stringed instrument, originating from the Indian subcontinent, used in Hindustani classical music.**
 
• The instrument was made of wood. It had a thin violin-type of the bridge and it was played by a plectrum worn on the right hand. It was invented by Amir Khusrau.

**Santoor **

 
• **The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer often made of walnut wood and has 72 strings**, which are struck with two delicate carved wooden mallets.
 
• The santoor is essentially a folk instrument that originated in the Kashmir Valley, and it achieved the status of a classical instrument due to the persistent efforts and genius of Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.
 
• **Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was an Indian famous classical musician, who attained international fame by playing the musical instrument, the santoor.**
 
• With his hard work, determination and talent, Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor a global name.

the cyclones from the Indian Ocean are obstructed by the Western Ghats
the Northeast monsoons pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and these winds are obstructed by the Eastern Ghats
the Northwest monsoons pick up moisture from the Arabian Sea and these winds are obstructed by the Western Ghats

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Coromandel Coast receive more rainfall in the retreating monsoon season than the normal rainy season.
 
• The retreating monsoon occurs when the winds become weaker and start to retreat back from the skies of North India to the Bay of Bengal. 
 
• As a result, the skies become clearer and clouds disappear. 
 
• The weather becomes extremely hot and humid because of which cyclones start emerging in the Bay of Bengal because of which the coast along the Bay of Bengal receives heavy rainfall. 
 
• It takes three months starting in mid-November and till January.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• November to January is also the period of tropical cyclones.
 
• This period is also referred to as northeast monsoon or winter monsoon as the northeastern states also receive rainfall during this time.

questions.question: Ullambana festival is primarily celebrated by which of the following communities in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhist.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ullambana is a festival primarily celebrated by the Buddhists following the Mahayana tradition.**
 
• Still, a number of Theravada Buddhists( **Laos, Cambodia, and Thailand**), too, celebrate this jubilee which lasts for around half a month- from the first to the fifteenth of the eighth month of the lunar timetable.
 
• This coincides with the month of July in the **Gregorian timetable.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The first day of the festival is considered the one when the Gates of Hell open and the ghosts are permitted to visit the earth for the **next fifteen days.**
 
• The fifteenth day is Ancestors Day and has the families visiting cemeteries to pay respect to their ancestors.
 
• People also make food offerings to the wandering spirit during this festival.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jain:**

 
 
• Jainism is one of the three most ancient persuasions of India, with roots that go back to at least the mid-first century B.C.E.
 
• Today, it's still an integral part of Indian culture.
 
• Jainism teaches that the path to enlightenment is through pacifism and reducing detriment to living effects( including shops and creatures) as much as possible.
 
 
 
• **Parsi:**
 
 
• The Parsis, also known as the Parsees, constitute a subsection of the larger Zoroastrian community who migrated to India from Persia in the 7th century AD during the Arab invasion of their homeland. 
 
 
 
• **Sindhi:**
 
 
• Sindhis are an Indo- Aryan ethnical group who speak the Sindhi language and are native to the province of Sindh in Pakistan.
 
• After the partition of the British Indian conglomerate in 1947, numerous Sindhi Hindus and Sindhi Sikhs migrated to the recently independent Dominion of India and other corridors of the world.

questions.question: The All England Championship, an international championship of badminton, was first held in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1899.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** All England Open Badminton Championships, or simply All England, is one of the world's oldest and most prestigious badminton tournaments.**
 
• Played annually, it developed after the success of the world's first badminton tournament held in Guildford in 1898.
 
• The tournament was successfully organized on April 4, 1899, however, only three categories (Men's Doubles, Women's Doubles, and Mixed Doubles) were originally staged.
 
• Both **Men's and Women's Singles were added the following year.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The first three events were named**" The Open English Championship".**
 
• It was ultimately considered( especially after the** first Thomas Cup series in 1949**) the unofficial world crown of the sport until** 1977 **when the **International Badminton Federation launched its sanctioned crowns.**
 
• The events were** halted doubly during World War I from 1915 to 1919 and World War II from 1940 to 1946.**

questions.question: Pandit Nehru said “Planning is a continuous movement towards desired goals”. He made this statement in the introduction of which Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pandit Nehru said “Planning is a continuous movement towards desired goals” in third five year plan which was incorporated during 1961 -1966 amidst two wars and a draught.
 
• This plan is also called **Gadgil Yojna,** named after the Deputy Chairman of Planning Commission, **D.R. Gadgil**
 
• The wars were fought between India and China in 1962 and between India and Pakistan in 1965.
 
• India was hit by drought in 1965 and 1966 across different parts of the country
 
• **The third five-year plan had set a target of a 5.6 percent growth rate but it could only achieve a 2.5 percent growth. **
 
• The lower growth rate during that period can be attributed to these natural and man-made calamities.
 
• The main target of this plan was to make the economy independent. The stress was laid on agriculture and the improvement in the production of wheat. 
 
• However, after the wars, India recognized the need to focus on the development of its defense sector. 
 
• After this combination of events, India had to face Inflation, which is a common term used for the rise in prices of items of common use.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Planning commission founded: 1950.
 
• Planning Commission head: Prime Minister
 
• First five-year plan launched: 1951
 
• A total number of 5 year plans: 12.
 
• Last five-year plan: 2012 to 2017 (Under PM Manmohan Singh).
 
• Planning Commission dissolved: 2014 (By PM Narendra Modi).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the function of a commercial bank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Regulating Money supply is done by Reserve Bank of India which is the authority to control inflation through monetary policies which it does by increasing:

__
 
• Bank rates
 
• Repo rates
 
• Cash reserve ratio
 
• Buying dollars
 
• Availability of credit.

On the other hand, Commercial Banks are banking institutions that accept deposits and grant short-term loans and advances to their customers. In addition to giving short-term loans, commercial banks also give medium-term and long-term loans to business enterprises. Nowadays some of the commercial banks are also providing housing loans on a long-term basis to individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 The primary functions of a commercial bank include:

__
 
• Accepting deposits:

 
 
• The most important activity of a commercial bank is to mobilize deposits from the public.
 
• People who have surplus income and savings find it convenient to deposit the amounts with banks.
 
• Depending upon the nature of deposits, funds deposited with the bank also earn interest.
 
• Thus, deposits with the bank grow along with the interest earned.
 
• If the rate of interest is higher, the public is motivated to deposit more funds with the bank.
 
• There is also the safety of funds deposited with the bank.
 
 
 
• Grant of loans and advances:
 
 
• The second important function of a commercial bank is to grant loans and advances.
 
• Such loans and advances are given to members of the public and to the business community at a higher rate of interest than allowed by banks on various deposit accounts.
 
• The rate of interest charged on loans and advances varies according to the purpose and period of the loan and also the mode of repayment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

In addition to the primary functions of accepting deposits and lending money, banks perform a number of other functions, which are called secondary functions. These are as follows:

 
• Issuing letters of credit, traveller's cheque, etc.
 
• Undertaking safe custody of valuables, important document and securities by providing safe deposit vaults or lockers.
 
• Providing customers with facilities for foreign exchange dealings.
 
• Transferring money from one account to another; and from one branch to another branch of the bank through cheque, pay order, demand draft.
 
• Standing guarantee on behalf of its customers, for making payment for the purchase of goods, machinery, vehicles etc.
 
• Collecting and supplying business information.
 
• Providing reports on the credit worthiness of customers.
 
• Providing consumer finance for individuals by way of loans on easy terms for the purchase of consumer durables like televisions, refrigerators, etc.
 
• Educational loans to students at a reasonable rate of interest for higher studies, especially for professional courses.

questions.question: As of 10 April 2022, who among the following is the senior most minister in terms of age among the council of ministers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Som Parkash.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The average age of the new council of ministers has reduced to 58 years from 61 years previously following a Cabinet reshuffle.
 
• **Nisith Pramanik (35), the Lok Sabha MP from West Bengal's Cooch Behar, is the youngest minister **to be sworn in, while the **oldest member in the council of ministers is 72-year-old Som Parkash.**
 
• There are** 77 members **in the Council of Ministers now.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Council of Ministers:**

 
 
• The Council of Ministers is** appointed by the President **on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• Typically, only members of Parliament are appointed as Ministers.
 
• The Council of Ministers consists of all orders of Ministers- **Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• His real achievement lies in bringing Cooch Behar out of the shadows of Kolkata and putting it on the national map.
 
 
 
• **Sudarshan Bhagat:**
 
 
• He's an active Indian politician belonging to Bharatiya Janata Party.
 
• He's a member of the Indian Parliament, and presently represents the **Lohardaga constituency.**
 
• He's the **Minister of State for Tribal Affairs **in the Narendra Modi government.
 
 
 
• **PP Chaudhary:**
 
 
• P.P. Chaudhary is the **Union Minister of State for the Law and Justice and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.**
